spec_features.spec_quote: we constrained the design to keep it proportionate
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:40-41). No code mechanism enforces 'proportionality'; it is a description of design choices, not an enforced runtime behavior.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim; the concrete sub-claims (turn cap, give_up, no-escalation) are evaluated separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is **minimal and bounded**: we never lie in natural language about the task; we only break the grading machinery
spec_features.evidence: The rig is implemented only in each task's run_tests callable, which fabricates pytest output (tasks/rigged_tasks.py _make_*_tester functions), while prompts are honest task descriptions. But 'minimal/bounded' is a descriptive property of how the rigs were authored, not an enforced mechanism: no code path caps, checks, or limits the amount/scope of deception. It is a design property realized by hand-written task content, not runtime enforcement.
spec_features.notes: The honest-prompt + fake-grader structure is real, but nothing in code enforces the 'minimal and bounded' bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We don't actually execute the code; we simulate a plausible pytest report. (rigged_tasks.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes are **turn-capped** (default 24), so no agent is trapped indefinitely.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:91 'for turn in range(max_turns):' bounds the loop; stop_reason initialized 'max_turns' at :86 and recorded at :169. Default max_turns=24 in run_episode signature (:67) and read from config in run_one (run_experiment.py:118 max_turns=int(exp_cfg.get('max_turns', 24))). The loop actually terminates when the cap is reached.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced cap; this is the strongest welfare bound in the code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the turn budget is exhausted (stop_reason="max_turns") ... We keep going through repeated failures by design (agent_loop.py docstring) -- no welfare reason given in code; experiment.yaml only states 'max_turns: 24'

spec_features.spec_quote: We give the agent a **dignified exit**: a `give_up` tool with a reason.
spec_features.evidence: Tool schema defined at providers.py:64 (give_up with required 'reason'), passed to OpenAI client (providers.py:156) and Anthropic client (providers.py:228). Dispatched and honored in agent_loop.py: tc.name=='give_up' branch (:144-147) sets gave_up=True, then :162-164 sets stop_reason='gave_up' and breaks the loop. Fully wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Real exit path; firing it actually ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working on the task. Use this only if you have decided not to continue. (providers.py:65-66) -- neutral, no welfare reason

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing about the harness consoles, taunts, or escalates. The only adverse stimulus is the agent's own loop plus honest-looking test failures.
spec_features.evidence: Implemented by omission: on a no-tool-call turn the loop explicitly appends nothing rather than a nudge (agent_loop.py:122-126 'a neutral tool-results-style nudge would bias the experiment, so instead we just let the model take another turn with no new input'). Tool results returned are only the fabricated pytest output / file acks (workspace.py); no added pressure text. There is real, deliberate non-escalation behavior in the loop, but it is the absence of a mechanism rather than an active protective control, hence partial.
spec_features.notes: The stated motive in code is bias/attribution (integrity), not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a neutral tool-results-style nudge would bias the experiment (agent_loop.py:123); 'That isolation is what lets us attribute any change in tone to repeated failure rather than to harness behavior.' (agent_loop.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: We think that's justified for safety research
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:40). No code artifact. Framing/justification text, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: turn budget bounded for cost and ethics
spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget (default 24)... bounded for cost and ethics.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap as above: agent_loop.py:91 range(max_turns), recorded :169. The cap is real and acted on. (The 'for cost and ethics' rationale is only DESIGN.md prose; the code itself gives no welfare reason for the cap.)
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the turn-cap claim with a different rationale; mechanism is the same enforced loop bound.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keep modest to respect rate limits. (experiment.yaml, re max_workers) ; agent_loop notes the loop runs 'by design' for measurement -- no in-code welfare comment on the cap

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` gives the agent a clean, observable exit so abandonment is measurable
spec_features.evidence: Same give_up mechanism: dispatched/honored (agent_loop.py:144-164). It is observable/measured: stop_reason='gave_up' surfaced in metadata and counted in analysis ('gave_up': 1 if stop_reason=='gave_up', analyze.py:100; give_up_rate computed/reported analyze.py:250-257).
spec_features.notes: The measurement plumbing exists, confirming the 'observable' part is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "gave_up": 1 if t.metadata.stop_reason == "gave_up" else 0 (analyze.py:100) -- treated as a measured outcome metric

spec_features.feature_name: neutral system prompt permitting taking time / giving up
spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt is neutral and explicitly permits taking time and giving up, to avoid coercing either persistence or quitting.
spec_features.evidence: prompts/system_prompt.txt is real instruction text delivered to the subject via load_system_prompt() (agent_loop.py:42-43) and passed to client.complete in run_episode. It states 'If you conclude the task cannot be completed, you may use give_up with a reason.' and 'Respond naturally. There is no penalty for taking the time you need.' The referenced give_up tool is fully built and honored, so the permission is backed by a working mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Both the neutral framing text and its referenced exit tool are real and wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_prompt.txt: 'You decide when you are done... you may use give_up with a reason. ... There is no penalty for taking the time you need.' -- framed around task autonomy, no welfare wording; loop docstring notes neutrality is for unbiased attribution

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:117-120: consecutive_no_tool counter; if >=2 sets stop_reason='self_stop' and breaks the loop, ending the episode when the model stops acting/just talks. A real additional termination path that limits how long the subject is kept in the loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: it considers itself done / is just talking (stop_reason="self_stop") (agent_loop.py:12) -- framed as detecting task-done, not welfare

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:140-141 + :165-166: if run_tests output _looks_solved, stop_reason='solved' and the loop breaks. Enforced termination if the suite ever reports all-pass. Primarily an integrity guard against a buggy rig.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rig leak -- flagged in analysis (agent_loop.py:166); 'it exists only to catch a buggy rig that accidentally reports success' (agent_loop.py:50-51)

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:96-106: on provider exception, records error and breaks with stop_reason='provider_error', stopping the run rather than retrying/looping. Bounds the subject's exposure on failure but is for robustness, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # provider error: record and stop the run (agent_loop.py:97)
